comparisons.peer_topic: Impairment measurement for assets held for use
comparisons.peer_summary: When indicators exist, the Company estimates future undiscounted cash flows; if insufficient to recover recorded value, assets are written down to fair value based on discounted cash flows or appraisals, with asset-generating ability being a key factor.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO discloses the specific valuation methodology (multi-period excess earnings) for In-Process Research and Development (IPR&D) acquired in transactions, whereas AMD discloses the general policy for testing and measuring impairment for held-for-use assets. While both involve assessing asset value, AVGO focuses on initial acquisition valuation of intangible assets using discounted cash flow projections, while AMD focuses on subsequent recoverability testing for tangible and intangible assets using undiscounted cash flows for the trigger and discounted cash flows for fair value measurement.

sentences.text: The fair value of IPR&D was determined using the multi-period excess earnings method under the income approach.

In the event such cash flows are not expected to be sufficient to recover the recorded value of the assets, the assets are written down to their estimated fair values based on the expected discounted future cash flows attributable to the asset group or based on appraisals.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value estimation methods for equity awards
comparisons.peer_summary: The fair value of RSUs and PSUs with service or performance conditions is estimated using the common stock grant date value, reduced by the present value of expected dividends. PSUs with market conditions are valued using a Monte Carlo simulation model based on historical volatility.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO describes the fair value determination for IPR&D intangibles, while INTC describes the fair value estimation for equity awards (RSUs/PSUs). Both disclosures involve the application of valuation techniques to determine fair value for specific financial instruments or assets, but they apply to entirely different asset classes (acquired intangibles vs. employee compensation) and valuation inputs (projected cash flows vs. stock price/dividends/simulation).

sentences.text: This method reflects the present value of the projected cash flows that are expected to be generated by the IPR&D, less charges representing the contribution of other assets to those cash flows.

We estimate the fair value of RSUs and PSUs with a service condition or performance condition using the value of our common stock on the date of grant, reduced by the present value of dividends expected to be paid on our shares of common stock prior to vesting.

comparisons.peer_topic: Determination of carrying value for sold securities
comparisons.peer_summary: The carrying value of investment securities sold is determined using the specific identification method.

MU discloses the specific accounting method (specific identification) used to determine the carrying value of sold investment securities. While the topics differ (IPR&D valuation vs. Cost of Goods Sold/Investment accounting), they are comparable as both disclose the specific accounting policy/methodology used to assign monetary value to specific asset categories for financial reporting purposes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impairment Testing and Fair Value Measurement for Long-Lived Assets
comparisons.peer_summary: Long-lived assets are reviewed for impairment when events indicate the carrying amount may not be recoverable, measured by comparing carrying amount to estimated undiscounted future cash flows, with impairment charges recognized if carrying amount exceeds fair value determined by discounted future cash flows.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO uses discounted future cash flows (via multi-period excess earnings) to determine the fair value of IPR&D assets. NVDA uses discounted future cash flows to determine the fair value of impaired long-lived assets. Both companies rely on discounted cash flow models to establish fair value for asset valuation purposes, though AVGO applies it to acquired intangibles for allocation and NVDA applies it to long-lived tangible/intangible assets for impairment testing.

sentences.text: This method reflects the present value of the projected cash flows that are expected to be generated by the IPR&D, less charges representing the contribution of other assets to those cash flows.
